You have also said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in my sight.’ 13Now, if I really stand in your favor, please show me your ways. Then I will know you, and I will go on finding favor with you. And keep in mind that this nation belongs to you as your people.” 14The LORD answered, “My own presence will go along, and I will bring you to rest.” 15Moses said to him, “Unless your presence goes with us, do not make us leave this place. 16How else will anyone know that you look with favor on me and on your people? Is it not by your going with us? That is what sets me and your people apart from every other people on the face of the earth.”

Moses asks to see God’s glory

17The LORD said to Moses, “This request too, the one you have just made, I will grant, because you have found favor in my sight and I know you by name.” 18Then Moses said, “Please, let me see your glory.” 19The LORD answered, “I will make all my goodness go past you, and I will announce the name ‘The LORD’ before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show compassion to whom I will show compassion.” 20He went on, “My face you cannot see. No human being can see me and stay alive.” 21The LORD said, “There is a place beside me. You are to stand there on the rock. 22While my glory is going by, I will tuck you into a cleft of the rock and shelter you with my hand until I have gone past. 23When I draw back my hand, you will see my back. But my face will not be seen.”
fields.summary: God tells Moses to lead the people on but says God will not go with them, and Moses meets God in a tent outside the camp. Moses pleads for God’s presence and asks to see God’s glory, and God agrees to pass by.

fields.title: Exodus 34
fields.body_html:
New tablets and the covenant renewed

1The LORD said to Moses, “Cut two new tablets out of stone, like the first pair. On them I will write the same words that stood on the first tablets, which you smashed. 2Be prepared for the morning. When it comes, climb Mount Sinai and take your place before me on its summit. 3Nobody is to climb with you, and nobody else may be seen anywhere on the mountain. Keep even the flocks and herds from grazing near the front of that mountain.” 4So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Early next morning he went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hand. 5The LORD came down in the cloud and took his place there beside Moses, and he announced his name, the LORD. 6The LORD passed in front of Moses and called out, “The LORD, the LORD, a God of tender compassion and grace, slow to grow angry, rich in faithful love and in truth, 7who keeps faithful love for thousands and forgives wrongdoing, rebellion and sin. Yet he will never acquit the guilty; he brings the wrongdoing of parents upon their children and grandchildren, to the third and the fourth generation.” 8Moses quickly sank down with his face to the ground in worship. 9He said, “Lord, if I really have found favor with you, then please, Lord, go in our midst. These are a stubborn people. Forgive our wrongdoing and our sin, and claim us as your own possession.” 10The LORD said, “Here and now I am making a covenant. In front of all your people I will work marvels such as have never been brought into being anywhere on earth or in any nation. All the people among whom you live will see what the LORD does, for what I am about to do with you will fill them with awe. 11Take care to keep what I am commanding you today. Watch: I am about to drive out ahead of you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. 12Watch yourself, so that you make no covenant with the people living in the land you are entering; otherwise it will become a trap set in your midst. 13Rather, you are to tear down their altars, shatter their standing stones, and chop down their Asherah poles. 14Bow down to no other god. The LORD is named Jealous; he is a jealous God. 15Do not make a covenant with the people who live in the land. For when they give themselves like prostitutes to their gods and offer sacrifices to them, someone will invite you, and you will eat from the sacrifice, 16and you will take some of their daughters as wives for your sons, and their daughters, prostituting themselves after their gods, will draw your sons after their gods in the same way. 17Do not make yourself gods cast from metal. 18Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread: for seven days your bread is to be unleavened, as I commanded you, at its set time in the month of Abib, because it was in Abib that you left Egypt. 19Whatever first opens the womb is mine, including every male firstborn among your livestock, of cattle or of sheep and goats. 20Every firstborn donkey you are to redeem by giving a lamb in its place; if you will not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you are to redeem every firstborn son of yours. No one is to come before me with empty hands. 21For six days you may do your work, but the seventh day you are to keep as a day of rest. Rest even when the fields need plowing or the harvest is ready. 22Keep the Feast of Weeks when the first of the wheat harvest comes in, and the Feast of Ingathering as the year comes round. 23Three times a year every male among you is to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel. 24I will dispossess nations to make room for you and push your borders outward. And while you are away three times a year, going up to appear before the LORD your God, no one will scheme to seize your land. 25When you slaughter a sacrifice for me, nothing leavened is to be offered with its blood. And nothing of the sacrifice of the Passover feast may be left over until morning. 26The choicest of the first produce from your land you are to bring into the house of the LORD your God. Never boil a young goat in the milk of its own mother.”

Moses’ face shines

27The LORD told Moses, “Put these words in writing, for they are the terms on which I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.” 28Moses remained there with the LORD for forty days and forty nights; he ate no food and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words. 29Moses came down from Mount Sinai holding the two tablets of the testimony. As he descended the mountain, he was unaware that the skin of his face shone with rays of light, because he had been speaking with God. 30When Aaron and all the Israelites looked at Moses, there was the skin of his face, shining, and they feared to approach him. 31Moses called them over, so Aaron came back to him, together with all the leaders of the community, and Moses spoke with them. 32After that all the Israelites came near, and Moses passed on to them as commands everything the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai. 33Once Moses was done speaking with them, he covered his face with a veil. 34Each time Moses went into the presence of the LORD to talk with him, he kept the veil off until he came out again. Then he would come out and tell the Israelites what he had been commanded to say. 35The Israelites saw the light shining from the skin of Moses’ face, and Moses would cover his face with the veil again until he went in to speak with him.
fields.summary: God gives Moses new tablets, proclaims the divine name as merciful and gracious, and renews the covenant. When Moses comes down from the mountain, his face shines.

fields.title: Exodus 35
fields.body_html:
Sabbath rest

1Moses gathered the whole community of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things the LORD has commanded you to do: 2There are six days in which work may be done, but the seventh day is to be holy for you, a Sabbath of full rest to the LORD. Anyone who works on it must be put to death. 3On the Sabbath day no fire is to be lit anywhere you live.”

Gifts for the tent of meeting

4Then Moses told the whole community of the Israelites, “This is what the LORD has commanded: 5Set aside among yourselves a contribution for the LORD. Everyone whose heart moves them to give is to bring it as the LORD’s contribution: gold, silver and bronze; 6blue, purple and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, 7rams’ skins dyed red, fine leather, acacia wood, 8oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense, 9and onyx stones and other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece. 10Every one of you who is wise of heart is to come and make all that the LORD has commanded: 11the tabernacle with its tent and its covering, its clasps, frames, crossbars, pillars and bases; 12the ark and its poles, the mercy seat, and the curtain that screens it off; 13the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence; 14the lampstand for the light with its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for the light; 15the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the doorway at the entrance to the tabernacle; 16the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand; 17the hangings of the courtyard with its pillars and bases, and the screen for the gateway of the courtyard; 18the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard, with their cords; 19the finely woven garments for service in the sanctuary, both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when they serve as priests.” 20Then the whole community of the Israelites went out from Moses. 21Then each one whose heart stirred them, and each one whose spirit moved them to give, came with the LORD’s contribution, to be used in building the tent of meeting, in all the service there, and in making the holy garments. 22They came, the men along with the women, all who had willing hearts, and they brought brooches, earrings, signet rings and pendants, every kind of gold object. Everyone who dedicated gold to the LORD as a wave offering brought it. 23And whatever blue, purple and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red and fine leather people had, they brought. 24Those who set aside silver or bronze brought it as a contribution for the LORD. People who had acacia wood that would serve for any of the work brought that as well. 25All the women who were wise of heart spun by hand, and they brought in the blue, purple and scarlet yarn and the fine linen they had spun. 26All the women whose hearts stirred them to use their skill spun the goats’ hair. 27The leaders brought the onyx stones and the other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece, 28and the spices and the oil for the lamps, for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense. 29The Israelites, every man and every woman whose heart moved them to give toward any of the work the LORD had commanded through Moses, brought it to the LORD as a freewill offering.

Skilled workers for the sanctuary

30Then Moses said to the Israelites, “Take note: the LORD has chosen Bezalel by name, the son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, 31and he has filled him with the Spirit of God, so that he has wisdom, understanding and knowledge in every kind of work, 32to think out artistic designs and to carry them out in gold, silver and bronze, 33to cut stones for mounting, to carve wood, and to do every kind of artistic work. 34He has also given the ability to teach to Bezalel and to Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. 35He has filled them with wisdom of heart to carry out every task of the engraver, of the designer, of the embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and of the weaver. They can do every kind of work and think out artistic designs.
fields.summary: Moses tells the people to keep the Sabbath and invites gifts for the tent of meeting. The people bring them willingly, and skilled workers are named for the work.

fields.title: Exodus 36
fields.body_html:
The people give more than enough

1Bezalel, Oholiab and every skilled person whom the LORD has gifted with skill and understanding, so that they know how to do every task in the service of the sanctuary, will carry out the work exactly as the LORD has commanded.” 2Moses called for Bezalel and Oholiab, along with all whom the LORD had made skillful, everyone whose heart stirred them to come forward and do the work. 3Moses handed over to them all the contributions that the Israelites had brought for the work of the sanctuary service, so that they could carry it out. Still the people kept bringing him freewill offerings every morning. 4So all the skilled workers who were carrying out the work of the sanctuary came, each one leaving the task in hand, 5and told Moses, “The people keep bringing more than enough for the task the LORD has commanded us to carry out.” 6Moses gave a command, and it was announced throughout the camp: “Men and women alike must stop preparing gifts for the sanctuary.” So the people were held back from bringing any more. 7The materials they had were enough for all the work, and there was some to spare.

Making the tabernacle curtains

8All the skilled craftsmen among the workers made the tabernacle from ten curtains of fine twisted linen and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim worked into them, the design of a skilled craftsman. 9Each curtain was about 42 feet long and about 6 feet wide; all the curtains had one measure. 10They joined five of the curtains to one another, and the other five they joined to one another as well. 11They put loops of blue yarn on the outer edge of the last curtain in the first set, and likewise on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set. 12They put fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty on the end of the curtain in the second set, so that the loops lined up with each other. 13They made fifty clasps of gold and joined the two sets of curtains with them, one to the other. So the tabernacle became one whole.

Making the tent of goats’ hair

14Then they made eleven curtains of goats’ hair to be a tent over the tabernacle. 15Each curtain was about 45 feet long and about 6 feet wide; all eleven had one measure. 16They joined five curtains together by themselves, and six by themselves. 17On the outer edge of the last curtain in the first set they put fifty loops, and fifty more on the edge of the joining curtain in the second set. 18They made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together so that it became one whole. 19They made a covering for the tent out of rams’ skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.

Making the frames and the inner curtain

20They made frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle, to stand upright. 21Every frame was about 15 feet high and about 2 1/4 feet wide. 22Every frame had two tenons, joined one to the other. They did this for every frame of the tabernacle. 23For the south side of the tabernacle they made twenty frames. 24Under the twenty frames they made forty bases of silver, two beneath every frame to receive its two tenons. 25For the other side of the tabernacle, the north side, they made twenty frames 26with their forty silver bases, two under each frame. 27For the back of the tabernacle, the west end, they made six frames. 28They made two more frames for the back corners of the tabernacle. 29They were double from the bottom and joined together at the top in a single ring. They made both corner frames this way, for the two corners. 30So the back wall had eight frames standing on sixteen silver bases, a pair beneath every frame. 31They also made crossbars from acacia wood, five of them for the frames along one side of the tabernacle, 32five for the frames of its other side, and five for the frames of the rear wall facing west. 33They made the middle crossbar to run halfway up the frames, reaching from one end to the other. 34They overlaid the frames with gold and made their rings of gold as holders for the crossbars; the crossbars too they overlaid with gold. 35They made the inner curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim worked into its design by a skilled craftsman. 36For it they made four pillars of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. Their hooks were gold, and they cast four bases of silver for them. 37They made a screen for the doorway of the tent from blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, worked in colors by an embroiderer. 38They also made its five pillars with their hooks. They overlaid the tops of the pillars and their bands with gold, and the five bases were bronze.
fields.summary: The people give more than enough, and Moses tells them to stop. The workers make the tabernacle’s curtains, the tent of goats’ hair, the frames and the inner curtain.

fields.title: Exodus 37
fields.body_html:
Making the ark

1Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood, about 3 3/4 feet long, about 2 1/4 feet wide and about 2 1/4 feet high. 2He overlaid it with pure gold on the inside and the outside, and put a gold molding around it on every side. 3He cast four rings of gold for it, set at its four feet, so that each side had two rings. 4He made carrying poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. 5He slid the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark could be carried. 6He made a mercy seat of pure gold, about 3 3/4 feet long and about 2 1/4 feet wide. 7He made two cherubim of gold, hammered out, for the two ends of the mercy seat. 8There was one cherub at this end and another at that end. He shaped the cherubim out of the mercy seat itself, at its two ends. 9The cherubim spread their wings out above, sheltering the mercy seat with their wings. They faced one another, with their faces turned toward the mercy seat.

Making the table

10He made the table of acacia wood, about 3 feet long, about 1 1/2 feet wide and about 2 1/4 feet high. 11He overlaid it with pure gold and gave it a gold molding all the way around. 12He gave it a frame about 3 inches wide on every side, with a gold molding all around the frame. 13He cast four rings of gold for it and set them at the four corners, one by each of its four legs. 14The rings were near the frame, to hold the poles by which the table was carried. 15He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, for carrying the table. 16He made the utensils for the table out of pure gold: its dishes, its pans, its bowls, and the jars used for pouring out drink offerings.

Making the lampstand

17He made the lampstand of pure gold, hammered out. Its base and its shaft, its cups, its buds and its blossoms formed one piece with it. 18Six branches came out from the sides of the lampstand: from one side three of its branches, and from the other side three. 19One branch had three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a blossom, and the next branch three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a blossom. It was the same for all six branches that came out of the lampstand. 20Four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and blossoms, were on the lampstand itself. 21There was a bud under each pair of branches that came out of it: one bud beneath each of the three pairs, for the six branches that came out of it. 22Their buds and their branches were part of it, the whole of it a single hammered piece of pure gold. 23He made seven lamps for it, along with its tongs and its fire pans, all of pure gold. 24From about 75 pounds of pure gold he made the lampstand and all its utensils.

Making the altar of incense

25He made the altar of incense from acacia wood, square in shape, about 18 inches on each side and about 3 feet high; its horns were part of the altar itself. 26He overlaid it with pure gold: the top, the sides all the way around, and the horns. And he ran a gold molding around it. 27Below the molding he made two gold rings for it, on its two opposite sides, as holders for the carrying poles. 28He made its poles from acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. 29He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of fragrant spices, prepared with a perfumer’s skill.
fields.summary: Bezalel makes the ark, the table, the lampstand and the altar of incense.

fields.title: Exodus 38
fields.body_html:
Making the altar of burnt offering

1He made the altar of burnt offering out of acacia wood. It was square, about 7 1/2 feet on each side and about 4 1/2 feet high. 2He shaped horns on its four corners, forming part of the altar itself, and overlaid it with bronze. 3He made all the utensils for the altar: the pots, shovels, basins, forks and firepans. He made all its utensils of bronze. 4He made for the altar a grating of bronze, worked as a mesh, and set it under its ledge, reaching from below up to the middle of the altar. 5He cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, to hold the poles. 6He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze. 7He slid the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar for carrying it. He built the altar as a hollow box of planks.

8He made the basin and its stand of bronze. The bronze came from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

Making the courtyard

9He made the courtyard. On the south side the hangings of the courtyard were of fine twisted linen, about 150 feet long. 10There were twenty pillars in twenty bronze bases, with hooks and bands of silver on the pillars. 11The north side was also about 150 feet long, with twenty pillars in twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the pillars. 12On the west side there were hangings about 75 feet long, with ten pillars and ten bases, and silver hooks and bands on the pillars. 13The east side, facing the sunrise, was also about 75 feet wide. 14On one side of the entrance there were hangings about 22 1/2 feet long, with three pillars and three bases. 15The other side was the same, so that there were hangings of about 22 1/2 feet on each side of the courtyard gate, with three pillars and three bases. 16All the hangings around the courtyard were of fine twisted linen. 17The bases of the pillars were bronze, and the hooks and bands on the pillars were silver. Their tops were overlaid with silver, and every pillar of the courtyard was fitted with silver bands. 18The screen for the courtyard gate was worked in colors by an embroiderer, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. It was about 30 feet long and about 7 1/2 feet high, matching the hangings of the courtyard. 19It hung on four pillars set in four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, and so were the overlay on their tops and their bands. 20All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard around it were bronze.

Metals used for the tabernacle

21This is the record of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, as it was counted at Moses’ command. The counting was the work of the Levites, led by Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. 22It was Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, who made all that the LORD had commanded Moses. 23With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and designer, who also worked in colors with blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.

24All the gold used for the work, for all the work on the sanctuary, was gold given as an offering. It came to about 2,200 pounds, by the shekel of the sanctuary. 25The silver given by those of the community who were enrolled weighed about 7,500 pounds, by the shekel of the sanctuary. 26That was about 1/5 ounce a head, half a shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary, from every man twenty years old and up who crossed over to join those enrolled, 603,550 men in all. 27The 7,500 pounds or so of silver went to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the curtain. There were 100 bases, and each took about 75 pounds. 28From the remaining 45 pounds or so he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their tops and fitted them with bands. 29The bronze given as an offering came to about 5,300 pounds. 30Out of it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar together with the bronze grating that belonged to it, all the utensils of the altar, 31the bases all around the courtyard, the bases of the courtyard gate, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the courtyard on every side.
fields.summary: The workers make the altar of burnt offering, the basin and the courtyard. The metals used for the tabernacle are counted.

fields.title: Exodus 39
fields.body_html:
Making the priestly garments

1Out of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, finely woven garments were made for service in the holy place. Aaron’s holy garments were made as well, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

2Bezalel made the ephod from gold, blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen. 3Gold was beaten into thin plates and cut into threads, which were worked in among the blue yarn, the purple, the scarlet and the fine linen with a designer’s skill. 4They made shoulder pieces for the ephod to join it together; it was fastened at its two ends. 5The woven band that went around it to fasten it was made the same way, in one piece with the ephod, of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses. 6They prepared the onyx stones, mounted them in settings of gold filigree, and engraved them, as a seal is engraved, with the names of the sons of Israel. 7Bezalel set them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Making the breastpiece

8He made the breastpiece with a designer’s skill, worked like the ephod, of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen. 9It was square. They made the breastpiece folded double, about 9 inches long and about 9 inches wide when doubled. 10They set four rows of stones on it. In the first row were a carnelian, a topaz and a beryl; 11in the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire and an emerald; 12in the third row, a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst; 13and in the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx and a jasper. They were mounted in gold filigree settings. 14The stones bore the names of the sons of Israel, twelve of them to match their names. Each was engraved like a seal with its own name, for the twelve tribes. 15On the breastpiece they made chains of pure gold, twisted like cords. 16They also made a pair of gold filigree settings and a pair of gold rings; the rings they put on two corners of the breastpiece. 17They tied the two gold cords into the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece. 18The remaining ends of the cords went to the two settings, which they fixed to the front of the ephod on its shoulder pieces. 19They made two gold rings and set them at the two lower ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge, the edge facing the ephod. 20They made another two gold rings and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, low on its front, near where it is joined, above the woven band of the ephod. 21They bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it lay on the woven band of the ephod and did not come away from it, as the LORD had commanded Moses. 22Bezalel made the robe that goes under the ephod, a weaver’s work, all of blue. 23The opening of the robe was in the middle, like the neck of a coat of armor, with a hem all around it so that it would not rip. 24On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of twisted blue, purple and scarlet yarn. 25They made bells of pure gold too, and put the bells between the pomegranates all the way around the hem of the robe. 26Bell and pomegranate, bell and pomegranate, they went all around the hem of the robe, which was worn for ministering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

27They made tunics of fine linen, a weaver’s work, for Aaron and his sons, 28the turban of fine linen, the decorative caps of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen, 29and the sash of fine twisted linen with blue, purple and scarlet yarn, worked in colors by an embroiderer, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

30From pure gold they made the plate that is the holy crown, and they engraved it, as a seal is engraved, with the words “Holy to the LORD.” 31To it they attached a cord of blue so that it could be fixed high on the turban, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

The work is finished

32In this way the whole work of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was finished. The Israelites carried out everything the LORD had commanded Moses; they did it all.

33Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and everything that belonged to it, its clasps, frames, crossbars, pillars and bases, 34the covering of rams’ skins dyed red and the covering of fine leather, and the curtain that screened the ark, 35the ark of the testimony with its poles, and the mercy seat, 36the table with all its utensils and the bread of the Presence, 37the lampstand of pure gold with its lamps set in a row, all its utensils, and the oil for the light, 38the gold altar, the oil for anointing, the spiced incense, and the screen for the doorway of the tent, 39the bronze altar with the bronze grating that belonged to it, its poles and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand, 40the hangings of the courtyard with its pillars and bases, the screen for the courtyard gate, its cords and tent pegs, and all the utensils for the work of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, 41and the finely woven garments for serving in the holy place: the holy garments for Aaron the priest and his sons’ garments for their service as priests. 42In every detail the Israelites had done the whole work as the LORD had commanded Moses. 43Moses looked at all the work, and there it was, done in every point as the LORD had commanded. And Moses blessed them.
fields.summary: The workers make the priestly garments and the breastpiece, as God commanded. The work is finished, and Moses inspects it and blesses them.

fields.title: Exodus 40
fields.body_html:
Instructions to set up the tabernacle

1The LORD said to Moses, 2“On the first day of the first month, set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting. 3Place the ark of the testimony in it, and screen the ark off with the curtain. 4Bring in the table and set out in order what belongs on it. Bring in the lampstand and mount its lamps. 5Place the gold altar for incense in front of the ark of the testimony, and hang the screen at the entrance to the tabernacle. 6Set the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting. 7Place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it. 8Set up the courtyard all around it, and hang the screen at the gate of the courtyard. 9Then take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy. 10Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils. Consecrate the altar, and it will be most holy. 11Anoint the basin with its stand, and consecrate it. 12Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water. 13Dress Aaron in the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him, so that he may serve me as priest. 14Then bring his sons forward and put tunics on them. 15Anoint them as you anointed their father, so that they too may serve me as priests. Their anointing will give them a priesthood that lasts for all time, through every generation.” 16Moses carried out all that the LORD had commanded him. That is just what he did.

Moses sets up the tabernacle

17In the second year, on the first day of the first month, the tabernacle was put up. 18Moses set up the tabernacle. He laid its bases, put its frames in place, fitted its crossbars and raised its pillars. 19He spread the tent over the tabernacle and laid the covering of the tent on top of it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

20He took the testimony and placed it in the ark, fitted the poles to the ark, and set the mercy seat on top of the ark. 21He brought the ark into the tabernacle and hung the curtain that serves as a screen, shutting off the ark of the testimony from view, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

22He placed the table in the tent of meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the curtain. 23He set out the bread on it in rows before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

24He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting across from the table, on the south side of the tabernacle. 25He set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

26He placed the gold altar in the tent of meeting, in front of the curtain, 27and burned sweet-smelling incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

28He hung the screen at the entrance to the tabernacle. 29He set the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

30Between the tent of meeting and the altar he placed the basin, and he filled it with water for washing. 31Moses, Aaron and Aaron’s sons would wash their hands and feet with water from it. 32Each time they went into the tent of meeting or came near the altar, they washed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

33He put up the courtyard all around the tabernacle and the altar, and hung the screen for the courtyard gate. So Moses completed the work.

The cloud and the glory

34Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the tabernacle was filled with the glory of the LORD. 35Moses was unable to go into the tent of meeting, since the cloud had come to rest on it and the tabernacle was full of the glory of the LORD. 36Whenever the cloud rose from over the tabernacle, the Israelites broke camp and moved on, at every stage of their journeys. 37If the cloud stayed where it was, they stayed too, until the day it rose. 38By day the cloud of the LORD rested over the tabernacle, and by night fire glowed within it. The whole house of Israel could see it, at every stage of their travels.
fields.summary: God tells Moses to set up the tabernacle, and Moses does everything as commanded. The cloud covers the tent of meeting and God’s glory fills the tabernacle.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
By day the cloud of the LORD rested over the tabernacle, and by night fire glowed within it. The whole house of Israel could see it, at every stage of their travels.

— Exodus 40:38

Exodus does not end in the promised land. It ends in the wilderness, at the foot of a mountain, with a tent and a cloud. The slaves are free, the covenant is made, and God has come to live among them. But the journey has hardly begun, and the last chapter says so: the cloud will rise, and they will move on, “at every stage of their journeys.”

The question the book leaves with you

The deepest question in Exodus is not whether God can defeat Pharaoh. It is whether a holy God can live among the people he has rescued. The book’s answer is yes, but at a cost, and not yet completely. At the burning bush Moses had to take off his sandals. At Sinai the people stood back at a distance and begged not to hear God’s voice. After the golden calf God said he would not go up among them, “since you are a stiff-necked people”, and only Moses’ prayer changed that. And in the very last scene, when the glory fills the tabernacle, even Moses cannot go in.

So the book leaves its readers with Moses’ own question: will God go with us? “Unless your presence goes with us, do not make us leave this place.” And with a second question hidden inside the first: how can sinful people come near to him and live? The next book, Leviticus, opens at the door of that tent, “From the tent of meeting the LORD called to Moses”, and spends itself on the answer.

Where the story goes next

The exodus became the pattern for every later rescue in the Bible. The psalmists sing it, the prophets promise a new one, and when the first Christians wanted to say what Jesus had done, they reached for its words. John writes that “The Word became flesh and made his home among us. We have seen his glory”, using a word that recalls the tent where the glory dwelt. Luke says that on the mountain of the transfiguration Moses and Elijah spoke with Jesus of “the exodus he was about to complete in Jerusalem.” Paul calls Christ our Passover lamb, and says of the rock in the wilderness, “and that rock was Christ.”

And the story ends where Exodus was always heading. In the last book of the Bible, those who have overcome stand beside a sea of glass and “sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb”, and a voice from the throne announces what the tabernacle only foreshadowed:

“See, God’s dwelling is with human beings! He will make his home with them, and they will be his peoples; God himself will be with them.”

— Revelation 21:3

Where to go from here

Exodus has fed Christian preaching, prayer and teaching for as long as there has been a church. A few places to begin in this library:

  • On the whole book. Hannah Whitall Smith’s Old Testament Types and Teachings, whose chapter “Exodus: God’s Redemption” reads the book as the story of God’s way of redeeming his people, set beside Romans 3.
  • On the God who hears the oppressed (Exodus 3). Absalom Jones’s A Thanksgiving Sermon on the Abolition of the African Slave Trade, preached in Philadelphia on 1 January 1808 on Exodus 3:7–8; and Gareth Evans’s Four Reasons We Need Revival in North America, which begins with Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3:1–6).
  • On the rock in the wilderness (Exodus 17). Christmas Evans’s The Smitten Rock, on 1 Corinthians 10:4, which follows the rock struck at Horeb to Calvary.
  • On the covenant and the Ten Commandments (Exodus 19–20). Andrew Murray’s The Two Covenants, whose chapter “The First Covenant” begins from Exodus 19:5; Thomas Watson’s The Ten Commandments; Martin Luther’s Large Catechism, which begins with the commandments one by one; and Book 2, Chapter 8 of John Calvin’s Institutes of the Christian Religion, “Exposition of the Moral Law”.
  • On the tabernacle (Exodus 25–40). Gareth Evans’s Burdens and Gifts (Exodus 25:40); and Horatius Bonar’s The Rent Veil, which moves from the veil of the tabernacle to the veil torn at the cross.
  • On Moses the intercessor (Exodus 32–34). E. M. Bounds’s Prayer and Praying Men, with its chapter “Moses, the Mighty Intercessor”; Andrew Murray’s The Inner Chamber, with “Moses, the Man of Prayer”; Gareth Evans’s Broken Before the Throne (Exodus 33:18–23); and A. W. Tozer’s The Hidden Life of Faith, on the cleft of the rock (Exodus 33:22).
  • On the faith of Moses. J. C. Ryle’s Holiness, with its chapter “Moses — An Example”, on Hebrews 11:24–26.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to Exodus in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this book.

And then read on, because the cloud is about to lift. The people who were carried out of Egypt on eagles’ wings still have a wilderness to cross, and they carry with them the promise Moses was given when he asked whether God would come:

The LORD answered, “My own presence will go along, and I will bring you to rest.”

— Exodus 33:14
